title: Santol Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Santol Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Santol nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen, potassium and phosphorus in santol, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Santol nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your santol turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, potassium, phosphorus and zinc. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.credit: Maja Dumat, CC BY 2.0, via Flickr

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, potassium and phosphorus move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But zinc stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which santol nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a santol nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest santol nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in santol

No santol particular description was found, so this follows general fruit tree signs. The whole tree turns light green, and the older leaves turn yellow, then brown, and fall. New shoots are short and thin, growth is slow, and the tree flowers and fruits less. You see it most at this stage: young trees in the first years after planting, and bearing trees after a heavy crop.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in santol
Trees that get no fertilizer or manure, sandy or eroded soils low in humus, and heavy rain that washes nitrogen down. Grass and weeds close to the trunk compete for it.
How to tell it apart

Santol leaves normally turn red or yellow just before they fall. The tree is partly deciduous, sometimes dropping most of its leaves at one time (ITFnet, PROSEA). To be sure, A leaf test of mature leaves from recent growth shows low nitrogen. New leaves that come out greener and bigger after a nitrogen dose confirm it.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency

PROSEA gives 100 to 200 grams of Ammonium sulfate 21 0 0 per tree in the first year, a month after planting and again before the rainy season ends. Young bearing trees get 200 to 500 grams of a complete fertilizer twice a year. Full grown trees need at least 2 kg of complete fertilizer per application. Use Complete 14 14 14, spread in a ring under the canopy edge and watered in or put on moist soil.

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (46 0 0), **YaraVera Viking Ship Granular Urea** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (46 0 0), **Planters Products Granular Urea** by Planters Products, Inc. (46 0 0) and **Harbest Granular Urea** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (46 0 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.
To keep it away, keep a weed free circle about 50 cm around young trees (ITFnet), mulch, add manure.
Potassium deficiency in santol

No santol particular description was found, so this follows general fruit tree signs. The edges and tips of older leaflets look burnt, and the scorch moves inward. Fruit size and quality drop, and the tree may suffer more from disease. You see it most at this stage: bearing trees, most of all during fruit growth.
Why potassium deficiency happens in santol
Sandy, leached soils under heavy rain, and years of fruiting with no potash returned.
How to tell it apart

Pink disease (Corticium salmonicolor), common on santol, forms cankers on branches. Fungal blights wilt and kill leaves on whole twigs and branches (PROSEA, ITFnet). To be sure, A soil test for potash and a leaf test.
What to apply for potassium deficiency

Feed bearing trees with Complete 14 14 14 at the PROSEA rates (200 to 500 grams twice a year for young bearing trees, 2 kg or more per application for full grown trees). Where the soil test shows low potash, add Muriate of potash 0 0 60 in split doses under the canopy, following the soil test.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Philphos Muriate of Potash** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Harbest Granular Muriate of Potash** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (0 0 60) and **Swire Muriate of Potash** by Swire Agrotech Agricultural Products Inc. (0 0 60). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, give a complete fertilizer every year from the first crop on, and return fallen leaves and prunings under the tree.
Phosphorus deficiency in santol

No santol particular description was found, so this follows general fruit tree signs. Growth is slow and the tree stays small for its age. Older leaves take on a purple color, most of all on the underside. You see it most at this stage: young trees after planting, and trees on poor acid soils.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in santol
Acid and eroded soils low in humus, and trees that get no phosphate at planting or later.
How to tell it apart

Santol leaves turn red before they fall as a normal habit. So look for the purplish tint on leaves that are still firmly attached and on a tree that is also growing slowly. To be sure, A soil test for available phosphorus and pH, and a leaf test.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency

Work Superphosphate 0 20 0, 16 20 0 or Ammonium phosphate 18 46 0 into the soil under the canopy, following the soil test, with manure or compost. For bearing trees, the complete fertilizer that PROSEA advises (Complete 14 14 14) also supplies phosphate.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (0 46 0), **Sagrex Duofos Granular Guano Phosphate** by Sagrex Corporation (0 22 0 (guano phosphate)), **Philphos 18 46 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0 (diammonium phosphate)) and **Atlas Di Ammonium Phosphate** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, put phosphate and manure in the planting hole, and lime very acid soils according to the soil test.
Zinc deficiency in santol

No santol particular description was found, so this follows general fruit tree signs. Zinc is the most widespread micronutrient shortage in fruit crops. Young leaves turn yellow between the veins and come out small, narrow and sometimes distorted. Shoots stay short so the leaves crowd in a rosette. Flowering and fruit size drop. You see it most at this stage: new flushes, when shoots grow fast.
Why zinc deficiency happens in santol
Sandy, leached soils, high pH or overlimed soils, and heavy phosphate fertilizer, which can hold back zinc uptake.
How to tell it apart

Gall mites (Eriophyes sandorici), the most serious santol pest, cause galls, bumps on the leaves, and stunted young trees (PROSEA). Zinc shortage gives small pale leaves without galls. To be sure, A leaf test for zinc and a soil test for pH and zinc. Spray a few branches and see whether the next flush comes out normal sized.
What to apply for zinc deficiency

No santol rate was found. Use a 0.5 percent Zinc sulfate spray (5 grams per liter) on several fruit trees, for example guava before flowering. So try it on a few branches of the new flush first. On soils proven low in zinc, add Zinc sulfate to the soil following the soil test.

Sold here with zinc: **Harvester Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Universal Harvester, Inc. (22 percent zinc), **Great Planters Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Agway Chemicals Corp. (21 percent zinc), **Zinc Sulphate Monohydrate** by Petbowe Trading Corporation (33 percent zinc) and **YaraVita ZINTRAC 700** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (40 percent zinc). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer with zinc](/blog/micronutrients-for-rice), and the page on [zinc deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/zinc-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, avoid heavy phosphate alone, and add compost or manure every year.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any santol nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your santol needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Santol nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my santol leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: A pale, light green tree with yellowing older leaves, short new shoots and a light crop. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at zinc deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in santol?
items.a: PROSEA gives 100 to 200 grams of Ammonium sulfate 21 0 0 per tree in the first year, a month after planting and again before the rainy season ends. Young bearing trees get 200 to 500 grams of a complete fertilizer twice a year.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes potassium deficiency in santol?
items.a: Feed bearing trees with Complete 14 14 14 at the PROSEA rates (200 to 500 grams twice a year for young bearing trees, 2 kg or more per application for full grown trees). Where the soil test shows low potash, add Muriate of potash 0 0 60 in split doses under the canopy, following the soil test.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes phosphorus deficiency in santol?
items.a: Work Superphosphate 0 20 0, 16 20 0 or Ammonium phosphate 18 46 0 into the soil under the canopy, following the soil test, with manure or compost. For bearing trees, the complete fertilizer that PROSEA advises (Complete 14 14 14) also supplies phosphate.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my santol lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the santol nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
